what: Fills the section background with a single color panel and wobbles the top and bottom edges (or just one) with 3D gradient noise — the edge undulates inward by the amplitude and drifts sideways (desktop frequency 3 · amplitude 1% of panel width · horizontal flow -.4/s · time .2, phone 3.8 · 5% · -.8 · .6). Stacked panels become color band boundaries. Draws only while on screen (WebGL shader)

options.edge: Shake edge — top · bottom · both, default both
options.freq · amp: PC frequency (waves across the panel width) · amplitude (ratio to the panel width), default 3 · .01
options.sp-freq · sp-amp: Frequency · amplitude at 767px and below, default 3.8 · .05
options.flow: Horizontal flow speed (negative goes left), default -.4 (phone -.8)
options.speed: Speed of the shape change, default .2 (phone .6)
options.--fx-band: Panel color (style or the consumer’s css), default var(--kf-accent)

use: <section data-fx="noise-edge-band" data-fx-noise-edge-band="edge: top; freq: 3; amp: .015" style="--fx-band: var(--kf-accent)">…</section>
note: The original draws several three.js planes onto a single canvas. The part uses one canvas per element, so no more than ten are attached on one screen (browser WebGL context limit is 16). The noise was rewritten with our own gradient noise — same grain as the original simplex, but each individual shape differs.

from.where: shared.js wave panel (WAVE_FRAG) · index.html [data-wave] section backgrounds (blue·red·cream·gold·purple, CONTENTS is five stacked panels)
